I'm 53 years old. I've been farming these fields since I was thirteen — forty years now. Never went to school, can't read, but I know my land. My wife and I work it alone. Our children left for the city long ago. We have 15 mu total, which is a good stretch of land for two people, but it means we work hard and can't afford to waste a single yuan.

I split the land two ways: **10 mu for wheat and corn rotation**, and **5 mu for cotton**. The wheat-corn is our backbone — it gives us grain to sell and some to keep. Cotton brings extra cash, but it's hard work with all the hand-picking. With only two of us, I have to be careful. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Old Wang down the road — he's a good farmer and if he changes something, I pay attention.

**Winter wheat on 10 mu:** I plant in early October, same as everyone in the village. I buy improved seed — about 30 jin per mu. Before planting, I spread a bit more than half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 60 jin. In spring, when the wheat starts jointing and looks a little yellow, I topdress with about 40 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: once before planting if the soil is dry, once at jointing in spring, and once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once in spring for weeds. For harvest, I hire the combine — it costs money but with only two of us, we can't cut 10 mu by hand. I expect around 800 jin per mu if the weather holds.

**Summer maize on the same 10 mu:** As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, we plant the corn — sometimes within two or three days. The window is tight. I buy hybrid seed fresh every year — can't save hybrid seed. I put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. If the corn looks strong and we get some rain, I might add 30 jin of urea when the corn is knee-high. I irrigate once or twice, usually at flowering if it's dry. Corn is easier to manage than cotton. I hope for about 900 jin per mu.

**Cotton on 5 mu:** I plant in mid-April. I put about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and add 30 jin of urea when it starts flowering. Cotton needs spraying — I spray three or four times for bollworm and aphids. I irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls are forming. Picking is the worst part. It takes weeks of bending over, and my wife and I can't do it all alone. I hire local women to help pick, pay them by the day. I expect maybe 400 jin of seed cotton per mu if the bugs don't get too bad.

Money is tight. I spend about what I spent last year — around 10,500 yuan on all inputs. I could buy more fertilizer, but what if prices drop at harvest? Better to be a little careful. I'd rather apply a bit too much than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps. That's how I've always done it.
